abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel topological framework for invariant visual pattern recognition that fundamentally reimagines how geometric features are extracted and matched in computer vision systems. Traditional approaches rely on metric-based representations that struggle with viewpoint invariance and occlusion handling. We propose a persistence homology-based representation that captures intrinsic topological features of visual objects, demonstrating that the birth-death dynamics of topological cycles provide a complete invariant descriptor. Our theoretical analysis establishes that this approach achieves theoretical guarantees for recognition under arbitrary projective transformations, something no existing method can claim. The mathematical foundation is built upon the theory of zigzag persistence modules and their stability under noise perturbations. We provide rigorous proofs demonstrating that the proposed topological signature is both computationally tractable and theoretically optimal for certain classes of visual patterns. Experimental validation on benchmark datasets reveals that this paradigm achieves unprecedented robustness to continuous deformations and partial occlusions. This work opens a new research direction that bridges algebraic topology and machine vision, suggesting that topological data analysis can provide the mathematical rigor that computer vision has historically lacked.

We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis of deep convolutional neural networks for 3D vision tasks, introducing a novel error bounds analysis that significantly improves our understanding of feature learning dynamics. While existing theories struggle to explain why deep networks excel at object recognition tasks, we derive novel bounds relating network architecture to representational capacity based on spectral analysis of the learned feature spaces. Our analysis reveals that the proposed attention-weighted pooling mechanism substantially reduces the VC-dimension of the hypothesis class while maintaining expressive power. We prove that this architectural innovation leads to improved sample complexity bounds, requiring fewer training examples to achieve equivalent generalization performance. The theoretical framework extends existing results on neural tangent kernel theory to handle spatially-varying receptive fields. Extensive experiments on 3D object classification and scene understanding benchmarks confirm that the derived bounds accurately predict practical performance gains. This work provides practitioners with actionable theoretical guidance for network architecture design in real-time vision applications.

This paper presents a paradigm-shifting architecture for industrial automated inspection systems that fundamentally rethinks the integration of heterogeneous vision sensors. Existing industrial vision systems suffer from rigid pipelines that poorly adapt to dynamic manufacturing environments. We introduce a novel neuromorphic-inspired event camera fusion framework that fundamentally differs from traditional frame-based approaches. The proposed system processes asynchronous visual events in real-time, achieving sub-millisecond latency for defect detection on high-speed production lines. Our architecture combines event-based cameras with structured light sensors through a learned attention mechanism that dynamically weights modalities based on scene complexity. The complete system integrates edge computing nodes for distributed processing, enabling scalable deployment across factory floors. Novel calibration procedures ensure geometric registration between modalities without manual intervention. Extensive validation on automotive assembly lines demonstrates that this new paradigm achieves 99.7% defect detection accuracy while reducing computational requirements by 60% compared to state-of-the-art alternatives. The event-driven paradigm fundamentally transforms how machine vision systems interact with the physical world.

We develop a practical system for vision-based robotic manipulation in unstructured environments that significantly advances the state-of-the-art in robotics vision applications. The proposed framework addresses the critical challenge of robust object pose estimation when dealing with specular, textureless industrial components. Our system combines a novel hierarchical attention network with a geometric verification module, achieving real-time 6-DOF pose estimation at 45 FPS on embedded hardware. The architecture incorporates a learned uncertainty quantification module that enables reliable gripper planning even with ambiguous sensor readings. We present a complete perception pipeline integrating 3D vision from multi-view stereo with depth sensor fusion through a novel confidence-weighted ICP algorithm. The system has been extensively validated in a collaborative robotics scenario requiring human-robot interaction, demonstrating safe operation with sub-centimeter positioning accuracy. Key contributions include a novel data augmentation strategy for training robust models and an efficient model compression approach enabling deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms. This work bridges the gap between research prototypes and production-ready robotic vision systems.
